description: Transcendental and root functions, and the domain guards that keep them finite.

cases.name: sqrt() of a negative is 0
cases.note: The argument is clamped to >= 0 rather than returning NaN.

cases.name: invsqrt() is the exact reciprocal square root
cases.note: MilkDrop ships the Quake fast-approximation here. This platform uses the exact reciprocal: strictly closer to the ideal, and identical across tiers.

cases.name: invsqrt() of zero or a negative is 0
cases.note: 1/sqrt(0) is Infinity, which the finite clamp zeroes.

cases.name: asin() and acos() clamp their argument to [-1, 1]
atan() of 1 is a quarter of pi
atan2() takes (y, x) in that order
cases.note: atan2(1, 0) is +pi/2. Swapped arguments would give 0.

cases.name: log10() of a power of ten is its exponent
exp() overflow reaches the store as Infinity and is clamped to 0 there
cases.note: exp() itself is NOT finite-clamped; the statement-boundary clamp catches it. The observable result is the same, but an implementation clamping inside exp() would differ for `exp(1000) - exp(1000)` (0 here, NaN-then-0 if clamped late).

cases.name: sigmoid() at zero is one half
